definitions.gloss: to invite, to ask to come

examples.japanese: {友人|ゆうじん}を{家|いえ}に{招|まね}いた。
examples.english: I invited a friend to my house.

examples.japanese: {結婚式|けっこんしき}に{親戚|しんせき}を{招|まね}いて{祝|いわ}った。
examples.english: We invited relatives to the wedding and celebrated.

examples.japanese: タクシーを{手|て}で{招|まね}いた。
{店員|てんいん}が{笑顔|えがお}で{客|きゃく}を{招|まね}いている。
examples.english: The staff member is beckoning customers with a smile.

examples.japanese: あの{発言|はつげん}が{大|おお}きな{問題|もんだい}を{招|まね}いてしまった。
examples.english: That remark ended up causing a big problem.

notes:
{招|まね}く is a transitive godan verb with meanings ranging from "to invite" to "to cause."

TRANSITIVITY:
- Type: {他動詞|たどうし} (transitive)
- Pattern: 〜を{招|まね}く

MEANINGS:
1. To invite (people): {客|きゃく}を{招|まね}く (invite guests)
2. To beckon: {手|て}で{招|まね}く (wave someone over)
3. To cause/bring about: {災|わざわ}いを{招|まね}く (invite trouble)

COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
- {誤解|ごかい}を{招|まね}く: to cause a misunderstanding
- {批判|ひはん}を{招|まね}く: to invite criticism
- {注目|ちゅうもく}を{招|まね}く: to attract attention
- {招待|しょうたい}する: to invite (formal)

CULTURAL NOTE:
{招|まね}き{猫|ねこ} (beckoning cat) is a lucky charm placed at shop entrances to invite customers and good fortune.
